name: comp-591

frames.best_why: The model menu is open with four options, their descriptions and a tick on the current one.

tagline: Switch AI models from a header button that lists each with a short description.
summary: A sparse dark chat header holding one model selector button on the left, with a bot icon and the active model name, and a temporary-chat icon plus user avatar on the right.
appearance: A dark header with a single ghost button at the left showing a bot icon, the model name Orion-Alpha 4.5 and a down chevron; at the right a dashed chat bubble and a round avatar. Opening the button shows a wide panel titled Models with four rows of name plus description.
behaviour: Clicking the model button opens a list of four AI models, each with a one-line description and a tick beside the active one. Choosing a model swaps the trigger label and closes the panel.
demo_content: Models are Orion-Alpha 4.5, Orion-Code 4, Nova-Chat 4 and Galaxy-Max 4, each with a short blurb.
use_when: A chat or AI product must let people switch model with the trade-offs visible.
avoid_when: Only four fixed models are listed, and the descriptions are static text with no pricing or limits.
customise: Model names, descriptions and the default are written in the file; the user menu is a separate piece.
weight_why: One select button, one icon button and a four-row menu.

a11y.note: The select and chat button are labelled, but the option descriptions are visual text and not announced as hints.

polish_why: Clear model list with useful one-line descriptions; the bar itself is very sparse.
